claims.statement: Zalo OA credentials are stored in the settings table (zalo.enabled, zalo.credentials) and pulled at runtime via a CredentialSource interface; ZALO_* env vars are bootstrap-time seed only and the admin UI at /admin/settings?tab=zalo is authoritative thereafter.

The zaloreset service is role-gated to employee and uses anti-enumeration via dummy sessions; the OTP login uses a Redis pending store (internal/infra/cache/otp_pending_store.go) with short TTL and atomic consume on verify.

OAuth v4 token refresh retries on -124 with exponential backoff; tokens refresh lazily on the next send rather than via a background sweeper so a fully idle OA stays connected without a heartbeat job.

Disabling Zalo (zalo.enabled=false) does not disable the OTP login or password reset endpoints — it only blocks the actual ZNS send, and the UI surfaces a clear error pointing users to the email path.

The Zalo client in internal/infra/zalo is stateless and DB-agnostic: it handles phone normalization, param clamping for ZNS templates, OAuth v4, and the -124 retry path; all state lives in calling services and the settings table.
